rules_text:
Rules summary Try to have the strongest dragons in the home areas. Playing a card Players take turns playing a card into a habitat on their side of the board either face-up or face-down. They can only play cards in areas that are not full. An area is full when it has 3 cards. When playing a card face up , it must match suit with the area it is placed in. When playing a card face down , it is not required to match suit . Players can only play a total of 3 face-down cards on their side of the board. After playing a card, the opponent must take the card on top of the area in which the card was just placed and add it to their hand. A new card is added to the area. Compare Strengths After playing a card into an area, compare the strengths . Players win an area by having the highest value of combined card value (only face-up cards) in that area. If so, move the claim token onto their side of the board. Otherwise, it stays where it is. Game end There are 3 ways to end the game . If a player has all 5 claim tokens on their side of the board – they win the game immediately. If a player cannot play a card – they lose the game immediately. If the game ends by both sides becoming full – players now r eveal all their face-down cards and check their strengths in each of the 5 areas. If the revealed card matches the suit it is added to the total value, if not its discarded. The claim token is moved to the side with the highest value. But if the value is double (or more) than their opponents, the area is lost and the other player gets the claim token instead. The player with the most claim tokens wins the game.

[Rating: 3/10] The concept is good but the rules need work. Losing the game because you can't make a legal play is nonsense when card draws are so random.

[Rating: 3/10] The game has a rule where if you double or more your opponent's score in a lane, then they win it instead.  This rule breaks and ruins the game.  Without it, it's just another unimaginative lane battler, but not as good as all the others that already exist.  Random on top of random.  Luck of the draw in multiple capacities.

[Rating: 4/10] After 2 games on BGA: Very simple rules, but a very tight duel. Too tight for my taste. It creates even more angst than Lost Cities. Players have to choose the least painful option available. Losing instantly when you can no longer make a legal move is extremely brutal. I still think there are some basic tactics I haven’t figured out yet. I don’t like the dragons, but the theme is pasted on anyway.

[Rating: 4/10] Not my kind of game (along the lines of Schotten Totten) but I can see some strategy if you get into this. The double and lose part doesn't jive with me though.

[Rating: 5/10] Feels like a Temu version of Lost Cities or Schotten Totten.  Generic dragon theme is cringe too.  Interesting how you can’t blame the luck of the draw because you essentially give your opponents specific cards.
